visuals.title: Where sarcoidosis strikes
visuals.text: Lungs and lymph nodes most often, but any system can carry granulomas.

visual.title: Chest X-ray
visual.caption: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, with or without pulmonary infiltrates.

visual.title: Scadding CXR stage
visual.label: Stage 1
visual.caption: Stage 1: BHL alone. Stage 4 is irreversible fibrosis.

visuals.title: When to start steroids
visuals.text: Parenchymal lung disease, uveitis, hypercalcaemia, neurological or cardiac involvement.

glossary.Multisystem: Affecting several organ systems of the body at once.
glossary.Lymph nodes: Small glands of the immune system that filter lymph and can enlarge in disease.
glossary.Afro-Caribbean: People of African or Caribbean descent; higher risk of sarcoidosis.
glossary.Facial nerve palsy: Weakness of the muscles of one side of the face due to facial nerve damage.
glossary.LMN lesion: Lower motor neurone lesion: damage to the nerve itself, so the forehead is also weak.
glossary.Parotid gland: The largest salivary gland, in front of the ear.
glossary.Lymphomatous infiltration: Invasion of tissue by lymphoma-like or lymphoid cells.
glossary.Serum ACE: Blood level of angiotensin-converting enzyme; raised in active sarcoidosis.
glossary.Transbronchial lung biopsy: Lung tissue sample taken through the airway wall during bronchoscopy.
glossary.Lung parenchyma: The functional tissue of the lung: alveoli and their walls.
glossary.Pulmonary infiltrates: Abnormal shadowing in the lung on X-ray from cells or fluid.
glossary.Interstitial infiltrates: Shadowing from disease in the tissue between the air sacs.
glossary.Pulmonary fibrosis: Scarring of the lungs that stiffens them and reduces gas exchange.
glossary.Pulmonary function tests: Breathing tests measuring lung volumes, airflow and gas transfer.
glossary.Spontaneous resolution: Getting better on its own, without treatment.
glossary.Oral corticosteroids: Steroid tablets, such as prednisolone, used to suppress inflammation.
glossary.Contraindicated: Should not be used because it could cause harm in that patient.
glossary.Neurological involvement: Disease affecting the brain, spinal cord or nerves.
glossary.Chronic respiratory failure: Long-term inability of the lungs to keep blood oxygen or carbon dioxide normal.
glossary.Non-necrotising: Without areas of dead tissue in the centre.
glossary.Macrophages: Immune cells that engulf and digest debris and microbes.
glossary.Multinucleate giant cells: Large cells formed by fused macrophages, with many nuclei.
glossary.Lymphocytes: White blood cells, mainly T and B cells, of the adaptive immune system.
glossary.Antigenic trigger: The substance that sets off an immune reaction; unknown in sarcoidosis.
glossary.Vitamin D: A vitamin made active in the kidney that increases calcium absorption from the gut.
glossary.Renal regulation: Control by the kidneys, here over vitamin D activation.
glossary.Intestinal calcium absorption: Uptake of calcium from food in the gut.
glossary.Mediastinal: Relating to the mediastinum, the central chest compartment between the lungs.
glossary.Immune-complex-mediated: Damage from antibody-antigen clumps depositing in tissues (type III hypersensitivity).
glossary.T-cell: A lymphocyte that coordinates or carries out cell-mediated immune responses.
glossary.Prognosis: The likely course and outcome of a disease.
